name: xff-prepended-last-incluster
why: An X-Forwarded-For chain prepends two external IPs, but the LAST sourceIPs entry (the apiserver's real TCP peer) is the pod IP 10.244.0.31. audit types.go: all but the last are client-settable, so the rule must trust only the last -- the anchored |re (...]$) tests the last element and the filter suppresses it, where a sourceIPs|cidr (a first/whole-element LIKE) would be fooled into firing. Proves the anchor.

name: non-pod-sa-token-off-source
why: A NON-pod-bound service-account token (minted by TokenRequest with no boundObjectRef, so no pod-name claim and no pod-name extra) used off-source. It shares the serviceaccount-username selection branch and the off-source last IP, but lacks the pod-name marker; adding pod-name is the single flip that fires the rule. Proves the rule keys on the pod-binding marker, not merely on a serviceaccount making an off-source call.

name: node-token-off-source-benign
why: A kubelet NODE token (system:node:, node-name extra, NO pod-name -- node-bound, not pod-bound) used from off-cluster. Ordinary node-credential activity that is NOT a pod-bound token: it must not fire this pod-token rule (the username is not a serviceaccount and there is no pod-name marker). Labelled benign (any shape) since it shares no selection item with the rule -- the non-pod serviceaccount near-miss covers the surface-sharing off-source look-alike.
